thread.title: OLED Display Suppliers Dim On Lowered iPhone X Prospects

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: OLED Display Suppliers Dim On Lowered iPhone X Prospects
text:
A report that Apple ( AAPL ) is pulling back on its shift to organic light-emitting diode, or OLED, displays for smartphones is hitting publicly traded companies involved in making the screens.
X Japan's Nikkei reported Monday that lackluster sales of Apple's flagship iPhone X handset "could result in a delay to the company's plans to introduce OLED screens in other models." Apple is widely expected to introduce two new OLED model iPhones this fall, along with a large-screen liquid-crystal display, or LCD, iPhone.
But disappointing iPhone X sales are leading Apple to consider boosting its production of traditional LCD-screen smartphones, while reducing production goals for OLED-screen iPhones, Nikkei said.
Universal Display ( OLED ), a key supplier of materials and technology for making OLED displays and lighting, has seen its stock tumble in recent weeks amid reports of slowing iPhone X sales. Two major equipment suppliers to OLED manufacturers — Applied Materials ( AMAT ) and Coherent ( COHR ) — also have been hit lately.
Universal Display shares were down 4.5% to close at 162.80 on the stock market today . Applied Materials lost 3.1% to finish at 55.33, and Coherent was 0.9% lower, near 266.61.
